questions.question: Define brute-force attack.
questions.solution_html:
• A brute-force attack is a method of breaking encryption by trying all possible keys until the

  • Identical plaintext blocks produce different ciphertext blocks.

  • Receiver receives the message and HMAC.

questions.question: Write the number of rounds in AES-128, AES-192, and AES-256.
questions.solution_html:
• • AES-128 → 10 rounds
  • • AES-192 → 12 rounds
  • • AES-256 → 14 rounds
  • Squeezing Phase
  • Encrypt the hash using the sender's private key.
  • Divide the block into Left (L) and Right (R) halves of 32 bits each.
  • Hides data patterns effectively.
  • Combine the key with the message using inner padding (ipad).
  • Uses the same secret key to compute a new HMAC.
  • Sender and receiver share a secret key.
  • CBC – Uses previous ciphertext block and IV.
  • Provides authentication and secure communication.

questions.question: State the need for digital certificates.

• Digital certificates are used to verify the identity of users, servers, or organizations and to
  • establish secure communication.

questions.question: Define substitution cipher.
questions.solution_html:
• A substitution cipher is an encryption technique in which each plaintext character is replaced
  • by another character according to a fixed rule.
  • Receiver decrypts the signature using the sender's public key.
  • After 16 rounds, combine the halves.
  • Resistant to pattern analysis attacks.
  • Combine the result with outer padding (opad).
  • If both match, the message is authentic and unaltered.
  • Advantages
  • • Ensures integrity.
  • • Provides authentication.
  • • Resistant to forgery attacks.
  • Essay type questions
  • Main issue: key distribution.
  • OFB – Uses keystream; no error propagation.
  • Supports integrity and non-repudiation.

questions.question: Define Stream cipher.
questions.solution_html:
• A stream cipher encrypts data one bit or one byte at a time using a keystream.
  • Receiver computes the hash of the received message.
  • Apply Final Permutation (FP) to obtain ciphertext.
  • Features
  • • Symmetric encryption algorithm.
  • • Uses 16 Feistel rounds.
  • • Widely used before AES.
  • Uses an Initialization Vector (IV) for added security.
  • Hash again to generate the HMAC value.
  • Examples: AES, DES, Blowfish.
  • CTR – Uses counter values; supports parallel processing.
  • Applications: SSL/TLS, digital signatures, secure email.
questions.final_answer: Applications: SSL/TLS, digital signatures, secure email

questions.question: Write the steps of key generation in RSA Algorithm.
questions.solution_html:
• RSA Key Generation Steps
  • Select two large prime numbers, p and q.
  • Compute:𝑛 = 𝑝×𝑞
  • Compute Euler's Totient:𝜙(𝑛) = (𝑝-1)(𝑞-1)
  • Choose an integer e such that:1 < 𝑒 < 𝜙(𝑛)
  • and gcd(e, φ(n)) = 1.
  • Compute d such that:𝑑×𝑒 ≡ 1(mod𝜙(𝑛))
  • Public Key = (e, n)
  • Private Key = (d, n)
  • • Public key is used for encryption.
  • • Private key is used for decryption.
questions.final_answer: • Private key is used for decryption

questions.question: Explain the concept of asymmetric key cryptography.
questions.solution_html:
• Asymmetric cryptography uses two different but mathematically related keys: a public key
  • and a private key.
  • Working
  • • The public key is shared openly.
  • • The private key is kept secret.
  • • Data encrypted with the public key can only be decrypted with the private key.
  • Advantages
  • • Solves key distribution problems.
  • • Supports digital signatures.
  • • Provides authentication and non-repudiation.
  • Examples
  • • RSA
  • • Diffie–Hellman
  • • ECC
  • Applications
  • • Secure email
  • • SSL/TLS
  • • Digital certificates
